chapter_title: Surface Area and Volume of Cylinders, Prisms, and Composite Solids

worksheets.title: Surface Area of Right Prisms and Cylinders

fluency_questions.prompt: Use Pythagoras' theorem to find any unknown slant edge or height first, then calculate the total surface area of each right prism:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Isosceles triangular prism with base $16\text{ cm}$, perpendicular height $15\text{ cm}$, and length $20\text{ cm}$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Right-angled triangular prism with hypotenuse $25\text{ cm}$, one leg $7\text{ cm}$, and length $12\text{ cm}$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Symmetrical trapezoidal prism with parallel sides $10\text{ cm}$ and $22\text{ cm}$, height $8\text{ cm}$, and length $15\text{ cm}$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Rhombus-based prism whose diagonals are $12\text{ cm}$ and $16\text{ cm}$, with prism height $10\text{ cm}$
parts.answer: $592\text{ cm}^2$ (rhombus side $= 10\text{ cm}$, end area $= 96\text{ cm}^2$)

fluency_questions.prompt: Find the exact total surface area (in terms of $\pi$) of each hollow or sector cylinder:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Hollow cylindrical pipe of length $12\text{ cm}$, outer radius $R = 5\text{ cm}$, and inner radius $r = 3\text{ cm}$ (including both annular end rings)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Cylindrical sector wedge of angle $\theta = 60^\circ$, radius $6\text{ cm}$, and height $10\text{ cm}$ (including the two flat rectangular faces)

parts.label: c
parts.question: Solid cube of side $10\text{ cm}$ with a circular hole of radius $2\text{ cm}$ drilled completely through from top to bottom

parts.label: d
parts.question: Closed cylinder whose height equals its diameter ($h = 2r$) with radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$

fluency_questions.prompt: Solve for the exact positive value of the pronumeral in each surface area problem:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Closed cylinder of height $h = 7\text{ cm}$ and total surface area $40\pi\text{ cm}^2$ (solve $2r^2 + 14r - 40 = 0$ for $r$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Closed cylinder of height $h = 5\text{ cm}$ and total surface area $48\pi\text{ cm}^2$ (solve $r^2 + 5r - 24 = 0$ for $r$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: Cube whose total surface area in $\text{cm}^2$ is numerically equal to $3$ times its volume in $\text{cm}^3$ ($6s^2 = 3s^3$)

parts.label: d
parts.question: Rectangular prism with dimensions $x, 2x, 3x$ and total surface area $198\text{ cm}^2$

fluency_questions.prompt: Calculate the total exterior surface area of each composite solid in exact form:

parts.label: a
parts.question: A rectangular barn $10\text{ m}$ long, $8\text{ m}$ wide, and $6\text{ m}$ high, topped by a half-cylinder roof of radius $4\text{ m}$ and length $10\text{ m}$ (including the flat floor)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Two solid cylinders of height $6\text{ cm}$: a top cylinder of radius $3\text{ cm}$ stacked concentrically on a bottom cylinder of radius $5\text{ cm}$

parts.label: c
parts.question: A solid cylinder of radius $6\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$ with a coaxial cylindrical recess of radius $2\text{ cm}$ and depth $4\text{ cm}$ bored into the top face (not all the way through)

parts.label: d
parts.question: An L-shaped prism of length $10\text{ cm}$ whose cross-section is a $6\text{ cm} \times 6\text{ cm}$ square with a $2\text{ cm} \times 2\text{ cm}$ corner removed

application_questions.question: A concrete culvert pipe under the Hume Highway is a hollow cylinder of length $8.0\text{ m}$ with external diameter $2.0\text{ m}$ ($R = 1.0\text{ m}$) and wall thickness $0.2\text{ m}$ ($r = 0.8\text{ m}$). Find the exact total surface area (inner wall, outer wall, and both annular ends) in terms of $\pi$.

A Norman window tunnel display is $5\text{ m}$ deep; its front and back cross-sections each consist of a rectangle $4\text{ m}$ wide by $3\text{ m}$ high topped by a semicircle of radius $2\text{ m}$. Find the exact total exterior surface area of the 3D solid.
application_questions.answer: $(94 + 14\pi)\text{ m}^2$ (two ends $= 2(12 + 2\pi) = 24 + 4\pi$, floor and two side walls $= (4 + 3 + 3) \times 5 = 50$, curved roof $= \pi(2)(5) = 10\pi$)

application_questions.question: A machine part is made by taking a solid steel cube of edge length $12\text{ cm}$ and drilling a circular hole of diameter $6\text{ cm}$ ($r = 3\text{ cm}$) right through the centre from the front face to the back face. Find the exact total surface area of the finished part.

A closed cylindrical chemical tank must hold a fixed volume of $128\pi\text{ m}^3$. If its radius is $r = 4\text{ m}$, find its height $h$ and its exact total surface area, and compare this with the total surface area if $r = 8\text{ m}$.
application_questions.answer: When $r = 4\text{ m}$, $h = 8\text{ m}$ and $\text{TSA} = 96\pi\text{ m}^2$; when $r = 8\text{ m}$, $h = 2\text{ m}$ and $\text{TSA} = 160\pi\text{ m}^2$ (so $r = 4\text{ m}$, where $h = 2r$, uses much less steel).

reasoning_questions.question: Prove that for a hollow cylindrical pipe of length $h$, outer radius $R$, and inner radius $r$, the total surface area (inner curved wall, outer curved wall, and two annular end rings) factorises neatly to $\text{TSA} = 2\pi(R + r)(R - r + h)$.
reasoning_questions.answer: $\text{TSA} = 2\pi Rh + 2\pi rh + 2\pi(R^2 - r^2) = 2\pi h(R + r) + 2\pi(R - r)(R + r) = 2\pi(R + r)(R - r + h)$.

reasoning_questions.question: A solid cylinder of radius $r$ and height $h$ is sliced into two congruent half-cylinders by a vertical cut through the diameter of its circular ends. Find the ratio of the combined surface area of the two half-cylinders to the original cylinder's surface area when $h = r$, simplified in terms of $\pi$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Original $\text{TSA} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r(r) = 4\pi r^2$. Cutting adds two rectangular cross-sections each of area $2r \times h = 2r^2$ ($4r^2$ total), giving $(4\pi + 4)r^2$. The ratio is $\dfrac{4\pi + 4}{4\pi} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{\pi}$.

parts.label: a
parts.question: The lower bound $A_{\min}$ and upper bound $A_{\max}$ of the rectangle's area

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

parts.label: d

parts.label: a
parts.question: The percentage error in the linear measurement $s$

parts.label: b
parts.question: The lower bound $V_{\min} = 9.95^3$ and upper bound $V_{\max} = 10.05^3$ rounded to $2$ d.p.

parts.label: c
parts.question: The percentage error of $V_{\max}$ relative to the nominal volume $1000\text{ cm}^3$ (to $2$ d.p.)

parts.label: d
parts.question: The percentage error of $A_{\max} = 6(10.05)^2$ relative to nominal surface area $600\text{ cm}^2$ (to $2$ d.p.)

application_questions.question: Water flows through a cylindrical irrigation pipe of internal diameter $10\text{ cm}$ ($r = 0.05\text{ m}$) into an empty cylindrical farm tank in Mildura of radius $2.0\text{ m}$ and height $1.5\text{ m}$. If water flows through the pipe at a speed of $2.0\text{ m/s}$, how many seconds does it take to fill the tank completely?
application_questions.answer: $1200\text{ seconds}$ ($20\text{ minutes}$, since $V_{\text{tank}} = 6\pi\text{ m}^3$ and flow rate $= \pi(0.05)^2(2) = 0.005\pi\text{ m}^3/\text{s}$)

application_questions.question: A solid metal cylinder of radius $4\text{ cm}$ and height $9\text{ cm}$ is submerged completely in a partially filled cylindrical beaker of internal radius $6\text{ cm}$. By how many centimetres does the water level in the beaker rise?

A trough of length $2.0\text{ m}$ ($200\text{ cm}$) has an isosceles trapezoidal cross-section with bottom width $30\text{ cm}$, top width $50\text{ cm}$, and slant sides $26\text{ cm}$. Use Pythagoras' theorem to find the perpendicular depth of the trough, and hence find its capacity in litres ($1\text{ L} = 1000\text{ cm}^3$).
application_questions.answer: Depth $= \sqrt{26^2 - 10^2} = 24\text{ cm}$; cross-sectional area $= \frac{1}{2}(30 + 50)(24) = 960\text{ cm}^2$; volume $= 960 \times 200 = 192\,000\text{ cm}^3 = 192\text{ L}$

application_questions.question: A density calculation uses $D = \dfrac{m}{V}$. A rock sample has mass $m = 300\text{ g}$ measured to the nearest $10\text{ g}$ ($295 \le m < 305$) and volume $V = 100\text{ cm}^3$ measured to the nearest $10\text{ cm}^3$ ($95 \le V < 105$). Find the minimum and maximum possible values of the density $D$ as exact simplified fractions.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why, when calculating the upper bound of a quotient $Q = \dfrac{a}{b}$ from rounded positive measurements $a$ and $b$, you must divide the upper bound of $a$ by the **lower** bound of $b$ ($Q_{\max} = \dfrac{a_{\max}}{b_{\min}}$) rather than dividing $a_{\max}$ by $b_{\max}$.
reasoning_questions.answer: A fraction increases when its numerator increases and when its denominator decreases. Therefore, to maximise $\dfrac{a}{b}$, you must pair the largest possible numerator $a_{\max}$ with the smallest possible positive denominator $b_{\min}$.

reasoning_questions.question: A rectangular sheet of metal of length $a$ and width $b$ ($a > b$) can be rolled into an open cylinder in two ways: either with circumference $a$ and height $b$, or with circumference $b$ and height $a$. Prove algebraically that rolling the longer side $a$ as the circumference gives the larger volume, by a ratio of $\dfrac{a}{b}$.
reasoning_questions.answer: If circumference $= a$, then $r_1 = \dfrac{a}{2\pi}$ and $V_1 = \pi\left(\dfrac{a}{2\pi}\right)^2 b = \dfrac{a^2b}{4\pi}$. If circumference $= b$, then $r_2 = \dfrac{b}{2\pi}$ and $V_2 = \dfrac{ab^2}{4\pi}$. Thus $\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \dfrac{a}{b} > 1$.
